properties.areaDesc: Tanana Flats; Eielson AFB and Salcha; Goldstream Valley and Nenana Hills; Chatanika River Valley; Two Rivers; Fairbanks Metro Area; Nenana; Northern Denali Borough; Southern Denali Borough
properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued October 17 at 2:54PM AKDT by NWS Fairbanks AK
properties.description:
A low in the Gulf of Alaska will will bring a front to the Alaska
Range and Central Interior Tuesday and Wednesday. There is
uncertainty with the exact strength and placement of this front
and we are currently expecting around 3 to 6 inches of snow from
the Western Alaska Range to Fairbanks. However, there is a 30%
chance for snow accumulations exceeding 6 inches in this area.
Currently, the greatest likelihood of this occurring is towards
Eielson AFB and areas east, where Winter Storm Watches are in
effect. If the front is a bit farther to the west, this chance
increases dramatically in/around Fairbanks.

There may end up being a west to east gradient where Eielson gets
6 inches or more of snow, and Fairbanks south/west only gets a
couple of inches. We will be monitoring this storm very closely
and will have more information as the details become clearer.

NWSheadline: Moderate to Heavy Snow Possible Tuesday and Wednesday

* WHAT...Urban area and small stream flooding caused by excessive
rainfall is expected.

* WHERE...Guam...

occurring. Rises in rivers and small streams.

moderate to occasionally heavy rain due to showers and possible
thunderstorms. This  is causing urban and small stream flooding.

properties.instruction:

deaths occur in vehicles.

enforcement and request they pass this information to the National
Weather Service when you can do so safely.

properties.areaDesc: Glacier Bay; City and Borough of Juneau
properties.headline: Hydrologic Outlook issued October 17 at 2:08PM AKDT by NWS Juneau AK
properties.description:
ESFAJK

A strong storm system is expected to move over the northern Alaska
Panhandle beginning Monday night and continuing through Tuesday.
Juneau and Gustavus are expected to see periods of moderate to heavy
rain for a majority of the day on Tuesday, resulting in significant
and rapid rises on small creeks and streams. Rain totals for this
event are around 2-4 inches over a 36 hour period, though expected
totals will likely change as the event moves closer. At this time,
expect to see similar impacts to the previous storm system we saw on
Friday, where Salmon River, Jordan Creek, and Montana Creek reached
either near or into minor flood stage. Additionally, ponding of water
on roads and areas of poor drainage is possible.

Stay tuned to weather.gov/juneau as we continue to assess the
situation and make updates to the forecast.

properties.areaDesc: City and Borough of Yakutat; Municipality of Skagway; Haines Borough and Klukwan; Eastern Chichagof Island; Cape Fairweather to Lisianski Strait; City and Borough of Sitka; Admiralty Island
properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued October 17 at 2:08PM AKDT by NWS Juneau AK
properties.description:
A strong storm system is expected to move into the northern half of
the Alaska Panhandle and the northeast Gulf Coast Monday night and
continuing through Tuesday. Beginning Monday night for Yakutat and
spreading eastward into early Tuesday morning, periods of heavy rain
will begin and continue through the day on Tuesday. For Yakutat,
Sitka, Pelican, and Elfin Cove, rain totals over a period of 36
hours is around 3 to 6 inches, with higher amounts near Yakutat and
lower amounts near Sitka. For the Icy Strait corridor, including
Hoonah and northern Admiralty Island, rain totals over the same time
frame are around 2-3 inches, similar to the previous storm. For
context, these totals are uncommon for this time of year, but are
not historically extreme.
